dedupe_keys.name: where will all the trees be australian urban green cover benchmark by local government area 2020

description: Where will all the trees be? is the 2020 update of the national benchmark of green cover in Australian cities and suburbs by the Greener Spaces Better Places programme, which is funded through the Hort Innovation nursery fund. The guide gives green cover and its rate of change for every urban local government area (LGA) in Australia, sets out trends since 2013, groups places into six kinds by rainfall, density and urbanisation, and names a best-on-ground LGA for each kind. The same data drives an online place finder by postcode, and related guides give canopy, shrub and hard cover by state and LGA (Where should all the trees go?) and the original 2014 canopy analysis. The guide is free to download from the page; no licence is stated. Caveats: it is a benchmark report with summary figures, not a spatial dataset, and the method details sit inside the download. Coverage is urban Australia. It supports climate adaptation and hazard exposure analysis for urban heat and stormwater, such as ranking council areas by tree cover when planning green infrastructure; related records are the Miami-Dade urban tree canopy statistics catalogued by another piece and the USFS urban forest inventory.
